title: Idempotents of B/IB lift after an etale neighbourhood of V(I)
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $A\to B$ a ring map with $B$ integral over $A$, and $\bar e\in B/IB$ an idempotent. Then there exist a ring map $A\to A'$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the induced map $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and an idempotent $e'\in B\otimes_AA'$ lifting $\bar e$: the composite $B\otimes_AA'\to B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B\otimes_A(A/I)=B/IB$ maps $e'$ to $\bar e$.

proof.text: *An annihilating polynomial.* Choose $y\in B$ lifting $\bar e$. Since $B$ is integral over $A$ and the image of $y$ in $B/IB$ is the idempotent $\bar e$, there are $d\ge1$ and a monic $f\in A[x]$ with $f(y)=0$ in $B$ and $f\equiv x^d(x-1)^d$ modulo $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-idempotent-annihilating-polynomial].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M4 (lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs), first two sentences (Lemma Tag 09XG)

proof.text: The elementary Bezout identity $1=X-(X-1)$ proves that $X$ and $X-1$ are coprime. Mathlib IsCoprime.pow proves the same for their $d$th powers, and $X^d$ is monic, hence has unit leading coefficient. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-coprime-factorization-etale] to obtain $A\to C$, etale and bijective modulo $I$, and $g,h\in C[X]$ factoring the image of $f$ and reducing to the prescribed powers.

Construct the canonical equivalence $B/IB\cong (B\otimes_A C)/I(B\otimes_A C)$ by the tensor-quotient equivalences and tensoring the quotient equivalence of $A\to C$; it sends the class of $b$ to the class of $b\otimes1$. In $T=B\otimes_A C$, put $y_1=y\otimes1$, $x=g(y_1)$ and $z=h(y_1)$. Evaluation is a ring map, so $xz=f(y_1)=0$. Reduction commutes with evaluation. Thus $x$ reduces to $\bar y_1^d=\bar y_1$, using idempotence and $d\ge1$. The two reduced values are coprime by applying the evaluation ring map to the coprime polynomial powers.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-make-tensor-pair-coprime] to $A,B,C$, the ideal $IC$ and the pair $x,z$. This gives a further etale $C\to D$ preserving its quotient, and a Bezout identity $1=u\,m(x)+v\,m(z)$ in $B\otimes_A D$, where $m$ is the map induced by $C\to D$.

Set $e=u\,m(x)$. The equation $m(x)m(z)=0$ implies $e\,v\,m(z)=0$, whence $e^2=e(e+v\,m(z))=e$. Compose the quotient equivalences of $A\to C\to D$ and obtain the canonical tensor quotient equivalence $\beta:B/IB\cong (B\otimes_A D)/I(B\otimes_A D)$, again checking its values on representatives. Write $t=\beta(\bar e)$. The reduction of $m(x)$ equals $t$ by functoriality of the quotient map. It is idempotent, and its product with the reduction of $m(z)$ is zero. Multiplying the reduced Bezout identity by $t$ yields $\bar u t^2+\bar v\overline{m(z)}t=t$, so $\bar u t=t$. Therefore the reduction of $e$ equals $t$.

The composite $A\to C\to D$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Take $A^{\prime}=D$, the composite quotient equivalence $\alpha$, and the idempotent $e$. The representative identities for $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and $\beta(\bar e)=e\bmod I$, give every clause of the unchanged Lean statement.
